column4: Razorpay and Paystack declare payment success from a bare client callback and discard the reference the gateway hands them
column5: Two of the four gateways treat the SDK success callback as proof of payment and forward nothing to the panel for verification. Razorpay registers handler: async () => at src/components/PaymentGateway/RazorPay.tsx:205 for the order flow and :149 for the wallet flow - the callback takes no argument so razorpay_payment_id and razorpay_signature which Razorpay passes to that handler are discarded rather than posted for checking. Paystack does the same at src/components/PaymentGateway/Paystack.tsx:140 with onSuccess: () => confirmSuccess() - and the reference and trxref fields it would receive are declared in the response type at :8 and :13 yet never read. Stripe in the same codebase demonstrates the correct shape: it calls stripe.confirmPayment at Stripe.tsx:77-85 and inspects the returned error and paymentIntent at :98-106 before treating the payment as done - so the success signal comes from the gateway API rather than from a fire-and-forget callback. WHAT IS VERIFIED HERE - the two callbacks discard the payment reference and no verification request is issued from the client. WHAT IS NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THIS REPOSITORY - whether the panel verifies the gateway webhook signature server side which is the control that actually settles payment state. The finding is the storefront total dependence on that unconfirmed control plus the loss of the reference that would let it cross-check.

column8: Anyone able to invoke the page callback in their own browser - the practical risk is a customer marking their own order paid in the UI rather than a third party stealing funds

column12: 1. Begin a payment through Razorpay or Paystack. 2. Invoke the registered success handler from the console without completing payment. 3. Observe the client proceeds to its success path having sent no reference to the panel.
column13: The gateway reference is forwarded to the panel and the success state is shown only once the panel confirms the payment - as the Stripe path effectively does by checking the returned paymentIntent.
column14: The client declares success from a callback that carries no proof and discards the identifiers that would allow verification.
column15: If panel webhook verification is missing or delayed the customer sees a paid state the backend has not recorded - and support cannot reconcile because the reference was never captured on this side. It also removes the storefront ability to detect a mismatch between what the gateway says and what the panel recorded.
column16: Capture the payment reference in both handlers and post it to a panel verification endpoint - showing success only on its response - matching the shape the Stripe integration already uses. Separately confirm with the panel team that webhook signatures are verified over the raw body and that events are deduplicated - and record that answer here so the dependency stops being an assumption.
